title: Rank-one derived difference model for countable ind-unipotent norm-coefficient modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. Put $A(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on the coherent profinite site [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], in compatible universes containing all profinite parameter sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be any profinite group (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group), and put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology. Use ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and condensed group actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Let $V_0\subseteq V_1\subseteq\cdots$ be a sequence of finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector spaces with injective $E$-linear transition maps. For every $n$, let $D_n:V_n\to V_n$ be nilpotent, meaning $D_n^{e_n}=0$ for some integer $e_n\geq1$. Assume the $D_n$ commute with transition maps. Give each $V_n$ a continuous $E$-linear $G$-action, compatible with transition maps and commuting with $D_n$. Give $H$ the action
$$t\cdot v=\exp(tD_n)v=\sum_{j=0}^{e_n-1}\frac{t^jD_n^jv}{j!}.$$
This is a finite sum, with $t$ mapped through $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset E$. Let $M_n(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V_n)$ with its finite-dimensional product norm topology, and use the induced $G\times H$-action. Form $M=\operatorname{colim}_{n\geq0} M_n$ in the category of internal $A$-modules with this action; this is a sheaf colimit, without completing its sections or imposing a uniform nilpotence bound. Let $D$ be the induced internal endomorphism and let $\tau=1\in H$. Thus $\tau-1=\exp(D)-1$ is an internal endomorphism of $M$, defined at every finite stage by the finite sum above.

Write $\Gamma_H^G:\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)\to\mathcal A_G(A)$ for the $H$-fixed-submodule functor retaining the $G$-action, with the inflation adjunction of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. In the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is an isomorphism
$$R\Gamma_H^G(M[0])\ \cong\ Q\bigl([\,M\xrightarrow{\ \exp(D)-1\ }M\,]\bigr)\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal A_G(A)),$$
where the displayed complex is in degrees $0,1$ and $Q$ denotes localization of complexes. The isomorphism induces in degree zero the identification of $H$-fixed sections with $\ker(\exp(D)-1)$ given by their common inclusion in $M$. The derived functor is the ordinary right derived functor in the full action category, not a derived functor computed only within the displayed class of modules. The assertion includes $G=1$, zero stages, $D_n=0$, and unbounded dimensions and nilpotence orders. For $F=\Omega$ the noncomplete norm topology and all continuous maps are retained.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] with $R=A$, $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $u(k)=k$ to form the actual morphism $c_M^G:R\Gamma_H^G(M[0])\to Q[M\xrightarrow{\tau-1}M]$. Forgetting $G$ takes this morphism to $c_M^1$ and reflects its invertibility. We therefore prove $c_M^1$ invertible for the original system with its $G$-action forgotten; this constructs the comparison before asserting any dense-restriction isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: construction of the relative cyclic comparison and conservative forgetting of the residual action; retained original proof step 1.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-trivial-procyclic-restriction-isomorphism], the actual scalar comparison $c_A^1$ is invertible, for either allowed $F$, and so are its finite trivial biproducts. Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-restriction-devissage] to every $(V_n,D_n,e_n)$ using this scalar hypothesis. It gives invertibility of each $c_{M_n}^1$ and identifies the finite-stage difference kernel with the fully $H$-fixed submodule. No common exponent or dimension bound is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar bar/evaluation base and finite nilpotent kernel-quotient induction; retained original proof steps 2-6, now carried by the trivial-procyclic and nilpotent-devissage nodes.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-profinite-invariants-filtered-continuity], forgetting the actions creates filtered colimits for both $G\times H$ and $H$; thus the forgotten original cocone has the same underlying sheaf colimit and is a colimit of $H$-modules. The induced $H$-actions agree on every coprojection, so this identification of colimits is $H$-equivariant. Apply [lem-sfb-filtered-cyclic-comparison-transfer] with $R=A$, $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $u(k)=k$, $I=\mathbf N$ and the forgotten diagram $(M_n)$. The index category is small and nonempty (it contains $0$); the maximum of any finite set of indices is a cocone. The transitions are $H$-equivariant since they commute with the $D_n$. Its actual coprojection cohomology square, including the zero negative degrees, shows that $c_M^1$ is invertible. Its colimit is the sheaf colimit in the statement, not a completed section space.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: passage to the original filtered sheaf colimit and the actual coprojection cohomology square; retained original proof steps 7-8.

proof.text: Conservative forgetting in [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] now makes $c_M^G$ invertible in $D(\mathcal A_G(A))$. At every stage $\tau$ acts by the specified finite exponential $\exp(D_n)$; the transition maps commute with these actions. Therefore its induced colimit action is $\exp(D)$ and the target differential is $\tau-1=\exp(D)-1$. This supplies the required derived isomorphism retaining $G$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: restoration of the residual G-action and identification of the differential with the stagewise finite exponential minus identity; retained original proof step 9.

proof.text: The invariant-inclusion normalization of [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] gives the required degree-zero map. Explicitly, a section of the sheaf colimit is locally represented at a stage; if its difference vanishes, refine locally to a later stage where the equation holds. The finite-stage kernel equality in [lem-sfb-nilpotent-restriction-devissage] makes that representative fixed after every base change and by every continuous $H$-parameter. Its colimit image is consequently fixed. Conversely an $H$-fixed section is fixed by $\tau$. Thus both subobjects have the same inclusion in $M$, including zero stages, $D_n=0$ and $G=1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: invariant-inclusion normalization and sheaf-local passage from finite-stage polynomial kernels to the colimit fixed submodule; retained original proof step 10.
